Bug_Details:
According to the J2EE specification, an EJB should not have any static fields
with write access. However, static read-only fields are allowed. This ensures proper
behavior especially when instances are distributed by the container on several JREs.
Examples:
public class SomeEJB extends EJBObject implements EJBLocalHome {

    private static int CountA;          // poor, field can be edited

    private static final int CountB;    // preferred, read-only access
}
Bug_Explanation: The static field 'CountA' is not final, which violate the specification of EJB. The bug is that the field can be changed from outside the class, which could potentially cause inconsistency and unpredictable behavior when instances are distributed by the container on several JREs.
